label: NIS2 Critical-Asset Risk Framework
description: Classify essential vs important entity status, build a critical-asset inventory, assess the Art. 21 cybersecurity risk-management measures and supply-chain security, and evidence Art. 20 management-body accountability under the NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555.

claudeKnowledge.description: NIS2 Directive (EU) 2022/2555; the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 on technical/methodological requirements of Art. 21 measures; national transposition acts (e.g. Sweden's cybersäkerhetslag, Germany's NIS2UmsuCG, Finland's Kyberturvallisuuslaki); ENISA guidance and the NIS Cooperation Group reference documents; ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and 27005; IEC 62443 for OT/ICS; the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847) for product security interfaces.

guidedInputs.label: Provisional NIS2 Classification
guidedInputs.description: How does the organisation expect to be classified under NIS2? Drives obligation depth, supervisory regime, and penalty ceiling. Leave as 'undetermined' if the classification itself is part of the scope.

options.label: Essential entity (Annex I + size threshold; ex-ante supervision)
Important entity (Annex II or medium-sized; ex-post supervision)
Believed out of scope (verify against Art. 2 + Annexes)
Not yet determined — classify as part of this assessment

guidedInputs.label: Primary Sector
guidedInputs.description: Which NIS2 Annex I (high-criticality) or Annex II (other critical) sector best describes the entity's core activity?

options.label: Digital Infrastructure / ICT service management (Annex I)
Digital Providers — marketplaces / search / social (Annex II)

guidedInputs.label: Jurisdiction(s) of Establishment / Operation
guidedInputs.description: Where is the entity established and where does it provide services? Determines which national transposition law and competent authority apply, and whether the main-establishment rule (Art. 26) concentrates jurisdiction.

guidedInputs.label: Assessment Scope
guidedInputs.description: Which parts of the NIS2 framework should this assessment prioritise?

guidedInputs.label: Environment & Asset Profile
guidedInputs.description: Describe the technology estate, critical services, key dependencies (cloud, MSPs, OT), and anything already known about the entity's NIS2 readiness.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Two regional data centres + Azure; a SCADA/OT network for substation control on an isolated VLAN; managed SOC outsourced to a Nordic MSSP; ~30 ICT suppliers, of which 4 are deemed critical. CEO sponsors security but the board has had no NIS2 training.

guidedInputs.label: Known Issues or Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Known weak spots, prior audit findings, supervisory contact, or incidents relevant to NIS2.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. No formal asset inventory beyond a CMDB that is ~60% complete; supplier contracts lack security clauses; last incident (ransomware on a non-critical file server, 2024) was never reported because reporting obligations were unclear; MFA not enforced for admin access to the OT jump host.

exampleInput: We are a Swedish regional electricity distribution operator (~600 employees, turnover ~€180m) preparing for the cybersäkerhetslag transposing NIS2. We expect to be an essential entity in the Energy sector (Annex I) and are also already designated under the older Swedish critical-infrastructure regime. Our estate spans two data centres plus Azure for corporate IT, and a SCADA/OT network controlling primary substations on segmented VLANs with some legacy RTUs that cannot run modern crypto. Our SOC is outsourced to a Nordic MSSP and we have roughly 35 ICT suppliers, four of which (the SCADA vendor, the MSSP, an Azure landing-zone integrator, and a billing SaaS) we believe are critical. Build us a critical-asset risk framework: confirm our essential-entity classification, produce a prioritised critical-asset and dependency inventory, score our maturity against the ten Art. 21 measures with particular attention to supply-chain security and OT, assess our Art. 20 management-body accountability and training gap, and tell us what our 24-hour/72-hour incident reporting flow to CERT-SE needs to look like. Known weak spots: no single authoritative asset inventory (the CMDB is ~60% complete), supplier contracts contain no security or audit clauses, and the board has never had NIS2 training.

exampleValues.environment_profile: Two regional data centres plus Azure for corporate IT; a SCADA/OT network for substation control on segmented VLANs with legacy RTUs that cannot run modern crypto; SOC outsourced to a Nordic MSSP; ~35 ICT suppliers of which 4 are deemed critical (SCADA vendor, MSSP, Azure integrator, billing SaaS).
exampleValues.known_concerns: No single authoritative asset inventory — CMDB ~60% complete. Supplier contracts lack security/audit clauses. The board has never had NIS2 training. MFA not enforced on the OT jump host. The 2024 ransomware incident on a non-critical file server was never reported because reporting obligations were unclear.
